payload.task: melting_point of n-eicosane (C20H42) with MACE-MPA-0, two-phase coexistence, production preset, T_guess 310 K
payload.reason: Premise check failed for this method/model/budget combination. (1) Model domain: MACE-MPA-0 is fitted to PBE/PBE+U inorganic bulk data (MPtrj + sAlex) with no dispersion correction. Solid n-eicosane is a van der Waals molecular crystal; its cohesion and fusion enthalpy (~68 kJ/mol, tier1.json) come almost entirely from interchain dispersion, which plain PBE barely captures. The MACE-MP authors themselves recommend adding D3 for molecular/vdW systems, and that would no longer be the requested force field. Without it the crystal is expected to be greatly underbound, so any coexistence temperature would be a model artifact that cannot be compared to the 310 K reference. (2) Validation: the same missing physics would spoil any independent check I could run, such as a shorter n-alkane melting point or the eicosane crystal density/sublimation enthalpy. So I cannot recover a known result before trusting a number. (3) Size and timescale: a defensible interface-pinned coexistence run for C20 chains needs several thousand atoms (62 atoms per molecule, plus a slab long enough for chain ordering at the interface) and multi-ns trajectories per temperature. Chain alkanes also pass through a rotator phase about 3-4 K below Tm (Velez 2015: 305.42 K), which makes the bracket harder to read. With MACE at that size and length, and my remaining compute/agent budget (<$1), I cannot set up, run and monitor this campaign. A short run would yield a superheating- or hysteresis-dominated number. Suggestion: if the team wants a MACE number, request MACE-MPA-0+D3 (or a molecular-trained MACE-OFF model) with a validation step first, e.g. the crystal density of eicosane vs tier1.json.

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the melting point of n-eicosane with the MACE-MPA-0 force field.
